terms.gloss: for the first time (with a word of time: tum, nunc, hodiē)
evidence: Cic. Rep. 2.12: lūdōrum grātiā quōs tum prīmum anniversāriōs in circō facere cōnstituisset (Lewis & Short s.v. prīmus)
Ter. And. 5.4.33: post illa nunc prīmum audiō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Usually with a word of time: tum prīmum, then for the first time; nunc prīmum, now for the first time; quō diē prīmum, on the day when first (Cic. Phil. 5.30, Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: at first; rarely, for the first time
evidence: Traupman 87: for the first time, prīmō
terms.comment: Lewis & Short: tum prīmum, “rarely prīmō”. Prīmō is mostly “at first”, as against later (see firstly); prīmum is the clearer word.

phrases.latin: pōnte sublicio tum prīmum in Tiberī factō
phrases.english: the Pile Bridge having then for the first time been built over the Tiber

sources: Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 87, 316, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.: p. 315.
